subject: psychology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the multi-store model, what causes forgetting from short-term memory when it is full?
questions.explain: When short-term memory is full, new information displaces existing items, causing forgetting.

questions.q: What is the approximate duration of information in the sensory register?
questions.explain: The sensory register holds information for only a fraction of a second to a couple of seconds before it is lost.

questions.q: Loftus and Palmer's car-crash study mainly investigated the effect of what on eyewitness testimony?
questions.explain: Loftus and Palmer showed that leading questions (changing the verb) altered witnesses' memory of an event.

questions.q: How is information mainly encoded in long-term memory?
questions.explain: Long-term memory encodes information primarily semantically, by its meaning.

questions.q: Forgetting because two pieces of similar information compete is called what?
questions.explain: Interference is forgetting that occurs when similar memories compete with and disrupt one another.

questions.q: In the working memory model, which component deals with speech and sound (the 'inner voice')?
questions.explain: The phonological loop deals with auditory and speech-based information, including the inner voice.

questions.q: Which type of long-term memory stores personal events and experiences?
questions.explain: Episodic memory stores personal events, episodes and experiences from one's own life.

questions.q: In Murdock's serial position study, recalling the LAST few words in a list best is called the what?
questions.explain: The recency effect is the strong recall of the final items, thought to still be held in short-term memory.

questions.q: In the working memory model, which component handles visual and spatial information?
questions.explain: The visuo-spatial sketchpad processes visual and spatial information, like picturing a route.

questions.q: A schema is best described as what?
options: A mental framework of knowledge that guides expectations
questions.explain: A schema is an organised package of prior knowledge that shapes how we interpret and remember information.

questions.q: How is information mainly encoded in short-term memory?
questions.explain: Short-term memory encodes information mainly acoustically, by the sound of the items.

questions.q: In the working memory model, which component is the attentional 'control' system?
questions.explain: The central executive is the control system that directs attention and coordinates the other subsystems.

questions.q: Bartlett's 'War of the Ghosts' study supports which idea about memory?
options: Memory is reconstructive and altered by schemas
Memory cannot be affected by culture
questions.explain: Bartlett showed memory is reconstructive, with recall distorted to fit existing schemas and cultural expectations.

questions.q: Forgetting where the cue is your internal state (such as mood) is called what?
questions.explain: State-dependent forgetting occurs when an internal state at recall does not match the state at encoding.

questions.q: How many stores does the multi-store model of memory (Atkinson & Shiffrin) have?
questions.explain: The multi-store model has three stores: sensory register, short-term memory and long-term memory.

questions.q: What is the widely accepted capacity of short-term memory?
questions.explain: Short-term memory holds roughly 7 plus or minus 2 chunks of information (Miller's magic number).

questions.q: In the multi-store model, what process moves information from short-term to long-term memory?
questions.explain: Maintenance rehearsal transfers information from short-term memory into long-term memory.

questions.q: In Loftus and Palmer's study, which verb produced the HIGHEST estimated speed?
questions.explain: The word 'smashed' produced the highest speed estimates, showing how question wording shapes memory.

questions.q: Why is eyewitness testimony sometimes unreliable, according to reconstructive memory?
options: Memories are rebuilt and can be distorted by schemas and later information
questions.explain: Reconstructive memory means recall is rebuilt and can be distorted by schemas and post-event information.

questions.q: In the serial position curve, recalling the FIRST few items well is known as the what?
questions.explain: The primacy effect is good recall of early list items, explained by their rehearsal into long-term memory.

questions.q: Which type of long-term memory stores skills such as riding a bike?
questions.explain: Procedural memory stores learned skills and how to perform actions, often without conscious thought.

questions.q: Forgetting due to a lack of suitable cues at recall is known as what?
questions.explain: Retrieval failure is forgetting caused by the absence of cues that were present at encoding.
